title: Low (1989), stiff crust over soft clays, published circle

meta.title: Low (1989), stiff crust over soft clays, published circle
meta.notes: Stiff upper slope on two undrained clays, the lowest with Su increasing linearly with depth (S = f(datum)), on the critical circle a commercial program prints with its Bishop value (center (18.001, 16.000), R 15.556).

source.reference: Low, B.K. (1989). Stability analysis of embankments on soft ground. J. Geotech. Eng. 115(2), 211–227; example 2, fig. 11.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V068 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Input audit 2026-10-24: the circle was (19, 18.5, R 18), on which cSlope gives 1.197; commercial program A's Fig. 23.3 prints center (18.001, 16.000), R 15.556 (end points (4.659, 8) and (33.557, 16)) with its Bishop 1.192. On that circle cSlope gives 1.134 (1.128 / 1.138 / 1.140 with 25 / 100 / 200 slices), and an independent spreadsheet Bishop calculation 1.13-1.15 (it depends on the slicing of the vertical scarp, since the center lies at crest level). The input agrees with commercial program A otherwise: its Ordinary value 1.370 on its Ordinary circle (Fig. 23.2: (17.201, 21.770), R 21.493) is reproduced by the same spreadsheet (1.374). So commercial program A's 1.192 is not reproduced on its own circle; cSlope's 1.134 is close to Low's Bishop 1.14, which is the check; commercial program A's 1.192 is not (as on V087, a program value that its own printed input does not reproduce). The circle's center lies at crest level, so its upper end is a vertical scarp: the factor depends on the slicing there.

2026-11-11: the steep ends of a circle are no longer cut into narrower slices (the maintainer's decision, DECISIONS.md), as in other programs. On this circle cSlope then gives about 1.161 (1.142 with the end cuts); Low's Bishop is 1.14 and commercial program A prints 1.192 on the circle. The difference comes from how the vertical scarp at the upper end is sliced, where Low calls the Bishop value misleading, so the problem is marked slicingSensitive (tolerance + 1 %, tolerance.ts) rather than keeping a finer slicing of the ends for this one surface.
